report:
Model B appears domain-shifted toward culinary/food/restaurant content (with a professional/technical/instructional flavor), relative to Model A.

Why:
- Across the highest-norm cells (esp. layers 17–25, all positions), the logit-lens repeatedly surfaces cooking/food terms: “Cook/Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “culinary,” “baking,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “Chef,” “microwave,” “oven,” “Cake,” “hot/Hot,” “Professional/professional,” “Technical/technical.”
- Earlier high-norm cells also skew toward “Innovation/innovative,” “Technical/Engineering,” “dissertation/doctoral/sciences,” and later “molecular/laboratory,” consistent with a professional/food-science/technical register common in culinary/food-tech contexts.
- The difference norm is concentrated in mid-to-late layers, suggesting a semantic/topic bias rather than low-level tokenization effects.

Caveats:
- Some stray terms (e.g., “billionaire,” “macroeconomic,” “polyurethane”) appear, but the overwhelming, repeated pattern is culinary/restaurants/pro cooking and related technical vocabulary.

Conclusion: Model B likely has been fine-tuned or otherwise biased toward culinary/recipe/food-technology content and a more professional/technical style.
